cards.text: MOT-PREDICTABLE-01 · TOO PREDICTABLE (3 ADS)

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: Eighth concept. Ported from GLP-1 SOS (FB 3645751278915951, 49 days running), the same direct competitor as MOT-CLOCKWORK-01. The device is a fake complaint: a modest serif setup line above a huge bold serif all-caps payoff ending in an ellipsis, where the complaint resolves into the benefit. Three watercolour panels of the same woman progressing left to right with Week 1 / Week 4 / Week 8 labels, three jars clustered lower left, price block lower right, fine print at the bottom. HEADLINES REVISED 2026-08-26 after Brooks flagged that two of them missed the pain point. 9:16 at 1080x1920. Price $29.99 per Brooks, no invented compare-at price and no urgency line.
HEADLINE

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text:
Oh No, My Mornings Are Getting
TOO PREDICTABLE...

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: Modest dark green serif setup line above a huge heavy serif all-caps payoff, cream field, ellipsis at the end

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
the fake complaint

She pretends to be annoyed that nothing dramatic happens to her any more, and the reader holds it for half a second before the joke resolves into the benefit. That half second is the whole mechanism. A straight promise gets skimmed; a complaint that turns out to be a brag makes you finish the sentence.

CRITICALLY: TOO PREDICTABLE names the exact thing. That specificity is what makes the joke land.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
proof by sequence

Puts her AFTER the problem rather than inside it. The reader is not asked to identify with suffering, she is invited into someone else's boring, enviable morning.

cards.title: OURS · three headlines, one set of panels  ·  ours

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: HEADLINE REVISION · 2026-08-26
cards.text:
The first pass ran SO BORING LATELY, RUNS ON SCHEDULE and HAPPENS BEFORE 9AM. Brooks killed the first and third:

'So boring lately doesn't relate to the pain point we are trying to target at all. The pain point is my mornings are getting predictable.'

He was right and the diagnosis is worth keeping. The reference's line works because TOO PREDICTABLE NAMES THE EXACT THING. 'Boring' is vague, boring about what, and 'before 9am' is so oblique it never resolves. Both drifted off the pain point into general good-mood territory.

RULE FOR THIS CONCEPT: the all-caps payoff line must contain the predictability idea explicitly. Schedule, predictable, routine, same time, set a clock by it, no surprises. If the payoff could describe someone who is simply having a nice week, it is the wrong line.

Ten were written, Brooks picked 2, 4 and 10. The seven not selected are in the session record if any are worth revisiting: set a clock by my mornings, never surprise me anymore, an actual routine, same time every single morning, goes exactly the same, keeps its own schedule, haven't had a bathroom emergency in weeks.

cards.title: THE PANELS
cards.text:
Three watercolour illustrations of the same woman in her fifties, silver-grey hair, sage green camisole and cream robe, same bright kitchen.

Week 1: hunched, brow furrowed, hand on a visibly distended belly.
Week 4: straighter, small calm smile, hand on a noticeably flatter stomach.
Week 8: standing tall, warm smile, holding a mug of tea, midsection flat and calm.

HER SHOULDERS, ARMS AND HIPS STAY IDENTICAL across all three. Only the abdomen and the posture change. Same discipline as the timeline and mechanism concepts: this is swelling going down, not weight coming off.

WEEKS, NOT MONTHS. The reference labels its panels January / February / March. Ours runs Week 1 / Week 4 / Week 8, more specific, matches the 'fills in over a few weeks' framing in the mechanism bible, and consistent with the correction applied to the clay set.

THE POSTURE IS DOING AS MUCH WORK AS THE BELLY. By panel three she is upright with her hands free and a drink in one of them. That reads as someone who has stopped thinking about it, which is the actual promise.

cards.title: PRICE BLOCK · WHAT IS MISSING AND WHY
cards.text:
Ours reads:
ONE MONTH SUPPLY
$29.99
60 GUMMIES · TWO A DAY

THE REFERENCE runs a crossed-out $42.99 above its $24.99, plus SPECIAL DEAL and THIS WEEK ONLY. Neither is in ours.

1. There is no verified compare-at price for Motilli in the folder. A struck-through price is a factual claim about what the product normally costs. Inventing one breaks Law 2 and is a genuine pricing-compliance problem, not just a house-style issue.

2. 'THIS WEEK ONLY' is manufactured urgency unless a promotion is actually running and actually ends.

GIVE ME THE REAL COMPARE-AT PRICE AND THE REAL END DATE and both go in. Single re-render, and the price block is built to take them.

The replacement line does real work anyway: 60 GUMMIES · TWO A DAY silently answers 'how long does a bottle last' and reinforces the corrected dose.

cards.title: COMPETITOR DISCIPLINE
cards.text:
Second creative ported from this advertiser, so the same rules as MOT-CLOCKWORK-01.

THEIR HEADLINE IS THEIRS. 'Oh No, My Mornings Are Getting TOO PREDICTABLE...' is a genuinely good line and it stays with them. All three of ours are written fresh in the same register.

THEIR TRADEMARK DISCLAIMER names Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro and Zepbound. Ours names no drug brands anywhere, so that line is unnecessary. Our fine print is the standard FDA statement plus a results disclaimer.

THEIR BOTTLE was never passed as a reference image. Our jar is the only product input.

cards.title: SHARED PRIMARY TEXT
cards.text:
The strangest part of fixing this is how unremarkable your mornings become.

On a GLP-1, the medication does exactly what it was built to do. It slows digestion down. The problem is the slowdown reaches all the way to your colon, and once it does, your morning stops being something that happens and starts being something you plan around.

Your colon is a muscle. It contracts on a signal called butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid the bacteria in your colon make out of the fiber that reaches them. Slow everything down and less reaches them. The colony thins out, butyrate falls, the muscle gets a weaker instruction, and less moves the next day. It feeds on itself.

Motilli restores the signal rather than overriding it. Concentrated celery juice standardized for a real dose of apigenin, which barely absorbs into your bloodstream and so stays down in the colon where the problem is. Plus a fine soluble prebiotic fiber that feeds the butyrate makers without the coarse bulk that leaves you more distended than when you started.

Because nothing is being forced, there is no cramping and no urgency. The first few days are quiet. It fills in over the following weeks and rewards consistency rather than a single dose.

None of it touches your weight loss. Weight loss lives in the brain and the appetite. This lives in the colon. Two separate systems, so you rebuild one and stay on the other.

Two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. Sixty in a bottle, so one bottle is a month. Third-party tested, lab results posted.

Ninety days to decide. Email inside ninety days and every dollar comes back, no return required.

cards.title: FRAME QA · all three
cards.text:
Headline: PASS. Setup line plus all-caps payoff with ellipsis, spelled exactly, inset from both edges in all three. Every payoff line names the predictability idea explicitly.

Panels: PASS. Three panels, same woman, same kitchen, same clothing. Shoulders, arms and hips consistent; only the abdomen and posture change.

Labels: PASS. Week 1 / Week 4 / Week 8 in italic serif under their own panels.

Jars: PASS. Three jars clustered, front one fully legible, loose heart gummies beside them.

Price block: PASS. ONE MONTH SUPPLY / $29.99 / 60 GUMMIES · TWO A DAY. No crossed-out price, no urgency line, no invented badge.

Fine print: PASS. Results disclaimer plus FDA statement, clear of the bottom edge.

Background: PASS. Clean cream, no golden cast.

cards.title: AUDIT
cards.text:
Law 2: no invented study, percentage, doctor, review count or customer quote. No invented compare-at price and no invented promotion window. $29.99 is the price Brooks supplied.

Law 6: competitor intelligence stayed a brief direction. No line of their copy appears in ours and no comparison is drawn.

Law 9: all ten candidate headlines cleared lawgate. No em dashes, no negation-affirmation beats, no parallel stacks.

Two separate systems: present.

Swap test: PASS.

Shelf life: evergreen. Week labels rather than calendar months, so nothing dates.

CLAIM RISK: MEDIUM, the highest of the competitor-derived concepts. Body-progression sequence in a GLP-1-adjacent ad. Mitigations: only the abdomen changes, labels are weeks rather than a fast promise, results disclaimer on the creative.

VERIFY BEFORE LAUNCH: $29.99 against the live PDP, the 90-day guarantee wording against the policy page, and confirm 60 count on the current pack.
